options: A real database hosted inside a SQL Server Database Engine instance that stores deployed projects, parameters, environments, and execution history
A standalone Windows service that runs separately from SQL Server
A folder on disk where .dtsx files are copied for backup
A feature of SSDT that only exists at design time
questions.explain: SSISDB is not a service or a special edition — it's an actual database, created inside a SQL Server instance, with a purpose-built schema and a UI on top of it in SSMS.

questions.q: Why must CLR integration be enabled before you can create the SSISDB catalog?
options: Because the catalog's stored procedures are implemented using CLR (.NET) code
Because CLR is required to run any T-SQL query
Because CLR integration encrypts network traffic to the catalog
It isn't required — it's just a recommended best practice
questions.explain: The SSISDB catalog is implemented with CLR stored procedures, so CLR integration must be enabled at the instance level or catalog creation fails.

questions.q: What does the master key password you enter when creating the catalog actually protect?
options: The database master key that SSISDB uses to encrypt sensitive parameter and connection manager values
The Windows login you use to connect to SQL Server
Nothing sensitive — it's only used to name the catalog
The SQL Server Agent service account password
questions.explain: The password protects the database master key used for encrypting catalog data, such as sensitive parameter values — it should be saved securely since it's needed to recover the catalog.

questions.q: What does a folder inside the SSISDB catalog contain?
options: One or more deployed projects and environments
Only SQL Server Agent job definitions
Only environment variables, never projects
A single package with no parameters
questions.explain: A folder is the organizational (and permissions) unit inside the catalog — each folder holds zero or more projects and zero or more environments.

questions.q: Where do you set catalog-wide settings like the encryption algorithm and how long execution history is retained?
options: The Catalog Properties dialog, opened by right-clicking SSISDB in Object Explorer
Inside each individual package's properties in SSDT
The SQL Server Agent job properties dialog
These settings cannot be changed after the catalog is created
questions.explain: Right-clicking SSISDB and selecting Properties opens the Catalog Properties dialog, which controls the encryption algorithm, operations cleanup, and project version retention for the whole catalog.
